newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - GE record Q4 profit tops $2 bln.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GE record Q4 profit tops $2 bln.

text.p: General Electric Co. , maintaining its place as the world's most profitable corporation, said Thursday it earned a record $7.3 billion last year as revenues and profit margins also hit new highs.

The nation's seventh-largest company said net income rose 11 percent to $7.28 billion, or $4.40 a share, from $6.57 billion, or $3.90 a share, in 1995. Sales grew 13 percent to $79.18 billion from $70.03 billion.
Profits in the fourth quarter grew 11 percent and surpassed $2 billion for the first time, GE said.

"The year's double-digit increases again demonstrate the ability of GE's diverse mix of leading global businesses to deliver top-line growth, increased margins and strong cash generation," Chairman John Welch said in a statement.
GE, based in Fairfield, Conn., said revenues grew at nine of its 12 major businesses, led by double-digit growth at NBC television, its Capital Services unit and its power systems division.
The company also said its operating profit margin improved to a record 14.8 percent of sales from 14.4 in 1995. Nine of the 12 business units reported higher margins, it said.

GE said fourth-quarter profits rose to $2.07 billion from $1.87 billion in the 1995 quarter. Earnings per share grew to $1.26 from $1.12. Its sales climbed to $22.99 billion from $19.75 billion a year earlier.
The company said per share earnings grew more quickly than net income due to the impact of shares bought back under a four-year, $13 billion repurchase program started in December 1994.
"The earnings are pretty much in line with expectations," said Steve O'Neil, an analyst at J.J.B. Hilliard, W.L. Lyons in Louisville, Ky.
GE's stock rose after the report but later fell back on profit-taking to end at $101.625, off $1, on the New York Stock Exchange.
Welch said he was "confident that GE enters 1997 better-positioned than ever to deliver another year of record profits."
GE spokesman Bruce Bunch said the company's diverse lines of business would continue to pay off.
"As we look ahead, we know we'll always have some businesses with very strong performance," he said.
"We obviously have seen great growth and success in GE Capital and NBC, which are service businesses, and now we're applying the service mentality to our industrial businesses," said Bunch.
"They're now moving beyond repairing products to providing solutions for their customers."
